newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. lawyer said eying other Italian firms - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawyer said eying other Italian firms - report.

text.p: U.S. lawyer Edward Gottesman, who led a consortium of investors who have agreed to acquire the ailing PC activities of Italian hi-tech group Olivetti has his eyes on two other troubled Italian companies, an Italian newspaper reported.

Milan daily Il Sole 24 Ore said Gottesman, who has helped set up a new company Piedmont International to take over Olivett's PC interests, is looking at bicycle firm Bianchi and fine porcelain maker Richard-Ginori.
Bianchi, one of the most famous names in Italian bicycle manufacturing with a history stretching back more than a century, has plunged into loss as the domestic market slumped.
Bianchi has a distribution agreement with Raleigh, the British bicycle manufacture controlled by Gottesman's main investment vehicle, Centenary Group.

Richard Ginori, has also run up losses, Il Sole said, adding that Gottesman's Cenetenary Group already owns British china maker Royal Worcester and may be interested in acquiring another company in the sector.
